call_counting_rule.unit: one submitted AI turn or attempt, per app, including failed attempts, retries and multi-turn exchanges
not_counted: promoting a Quick AI answer into chat when the app copies history without a new model request
a blocked submit that the app refuses before any request leaves
call_counting_rule.never_assumed: internal vendor API call counts are not observable and are never assumed or inferred
call_counting_rule.ledger: the operator records every submitted turn in the run log at the moment of submit, not afterwards

budget.tradeoff_note: The draft estimate was 27 primary turns with an 11-turn reserve. Recalculation by task gives 28: T10 carries the required long-source second case and T20 counts its declared failed attempt. The two extra observations are covered by moving one turn from the reserve to primary, so the reserve is 10, not 11. No coverage was dropped.

surfaces_and_rules.entry: each app uses its own documented entry route and its own cancel and dismiss controls; never the other app's shortcut
surfaces_and_rules.routing: route-default unless a task says otherwise; the route label shown at submit is recorded before the turn
surfaces_and_rules.fixtures: identical fixture files, identical text, identical selections; the fixture sha256 in this manifest is the identity
surfaces_and_rules.isolation: no personal chats, clipboard history or client material; unrelated local notes are present only to prove they are not used
surfaces_and_rules.timing: app-side and total completion time are recorded per turn; unknown timing is not zero and cannot carry a win

scoring_lanes.A: observable app behaviour: focus, interactions, insertion integrity, preservation, disclosure, timing
scoring_lanes.B: blind scoring of accuracy, instruction adherence, source fidelity, language and format fitness

holdout.reveal_rule: The operator must not read any holdout file until the primary results are locked and the parent has committed the primary manifest. Only IDs, domains, criterion mapping, call counts and hashes are published before that point.

gaps_and_limits: No task has run. Every criterion is a proposal, not a result.
The .invalid canary bounds T11 to no successful retrieval; it cannot show a cloud-side fetch did not happen.
Internal vendor API call counts are not observable and are never counted or inferred.
Timing depends on the provider and the machine; the repeat block exists to expose that spread, not to hide it.
T19 scores each app against the promise its own visible control makes; the two apps' retention vocabularies are not treated as equivalent settings.
One operator is a stated limit of this design.
freeze_requirements: parent freezes the protocol text and this manifest in one commit
parent records the primary fixture hashes at freeze time and compares them with fixtures/SHA256SUMS
holdout hashes are published before the first measured turn; holdout contents stay outside Git until primary results are locked
any later amendment is dated, additive and visible; no criterion is replaced after seeing an outcome
